utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Harvey, are you ready to continue cross-examination of Witness 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Witness 6, I want to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony; that is, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness 6.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When we left off on Friday, I had asked you about a visit that you made to Jagodina, and I'd like to start back there this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have, with the assistance of my colleagues, managed to prepare a map over the weekend. It hasn't been possible to upload it into e-court yet. Your Honour, I see, has it. Perhaps the witness could be shown a copy of it, and probably the best thing would be if it could be placed on the ELMO. Now we have it up on the screens. Could it move just a fraction out, just a tiny little bit more. That's it, perfect. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, Witness 6, do you see the map on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And if you look all the way to the bottom of the map, do you see Djakovica is marked there? Perhaps -- well, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I don't know if Madam Usher can assist you. It's almost at the very bottom, about a third -- between a third and a half from the centre. There we go. Yeah. Okay. And you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Sorry. Get a translation of that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat what you just said, because the interpreters did not hear you correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did see it. I can see Gjakove on the map, Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And do you see Beograd at the top left-hand corner of the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, if you take a direction to the south-west of Beograd, can you find Jagodina on that map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Harvey, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: My apologies. Again, could I ask that we pull back from this picture just a little so that we can see the scale that is shown at the bottom of the map. A bit further. Yeah. There we are. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, do you see, sir, to the bottom right-hand corner there is a scale of 100 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the distance by road between Djakovica and Jagodina would be something in the region of 250 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You drove that journey, didn't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but I didn't mark down the kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: On how many occasions have you made that journey, sir, to Jagodina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And when you went there last year, that was to renew your driver's licence, your Serbian driver's licence, and to obtain some travel documents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I went to get some citizenship papers and to renew the driver's licence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And was there any other purpose for which you went there, sir, last year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brothers wanted to have their citizenship papers because they work abroad and they needed for the Swiss consulate, they needed those papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You could have obtained the same papers in Pristina, could you not, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we're not a state yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You can obtain travel documents in Pristina, can't you? You can obtain Schengen visas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I went there to get those papers, to renew the Yugoslav passports for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, your question about getting visas and getting travel documents is rather confusing. As far as my legal knowledge goes, if I want to apply for a visa, that is, entry into a certain country, I have to approach the authorities of that country or that area. Whereas if I -- so, for example, if I want to enter the United States, I need a visa -- I don't need it anymore at this moment, but I would have to go to the US consulate whereas if you want to have a new passport I would go to my own authorities. So therefore to say you could get travel papers, isn't it, in Pristina, you could get visa, Schengen visa, that is confusing for me and it might be confusing for the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I apologise for any confusion. Let me see if I can resolve it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do the Swiss authorities, that is, the Swiss government maintain a consulate in Jagodina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So you weren't going to Jagodina to obtain any papers -- any visas issued by the Swiss authorities, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How many passports do you hold, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one, a Yugoslav one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How many driving licences do you hold, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the one from UNMIK.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I thought you told us that you went to Jagodina to obtain a driving licence there, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but they did not give it to me. They said, Come back in three months, and I didn't go to get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And so, please tell us, what are the papers for your brothers in Switzerland that you were going to collect in Jagodina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're Yugoslav citizenship papers, in order for their passports to be renewed in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And what is the office that you went to in Jagodina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the centre of SUP, of Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Is this the only time you've been to that office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Madam Registrar, perhaps before I move on we should mark this -- have this map marked for identification, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I do not mind to have it marked; at the same time, it has assisted us in knowing where we approximately are. But apart from that, it's a map as any other map, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm in Your Honours hands. I think that's probably true. The record speaks for itself in terms of -- the only matter that I would seek to introduce it for, since the witness has indicated that he does not know the distance in kilometres between Gjakove and Jagodina --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Madam Registrar, it would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D113.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. No objections against admission? I take it that you want to tender it, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D113 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, moving on to your interview in Jagodina, you gave a sworn statement to the commander of the SUP in Jagodina; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You swore in that statement to tell the truth; that's correct, yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I think it would probably assist us to have 3D010174 on the screens, it would assist the witness to have -- well, it probably won't assist the witness because we don't have a translation in a language that he understands, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: While that's being brought up, Witness 6 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Mr. Harvey, one question: The Chamber has been provided with copies of statements, as usual. I noticed that the original we received is not exactly the same as the translation we have on our screen at this moment. Of course, I didn't check the whole of it, but it struck me that under the date, the 11th of July, 2006, in my original I see something which very much looks like IKM Jagodina, Jagodina, which does not appear on the translation. Of course, I'm not in a position to check translations in full, but there seems to be a -- I don't know whether you have the same original. That's with a -- with a finger-mark on the bottom --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I have everything Your Honour has, and before we go any further perhaps since this document may reveal more than ought to be in the public domain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we should --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- we should be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we should be in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I apologise I --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: This statement was taken in Jagodina, you've just confirmed, if that's witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It was taken in the SUP office, the Secretariat of the Interior, which purports to exercise authority over the area of Gjakove/Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there to get those documents. I don't know about the other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: What is your understanding about that office in Jagodina? Do they issue papers for people who live in Gjakove or Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Most of the people went there to get their documents; I went, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: There's no SUP office at this time or last year in Gjakove, is there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you said you came to Gjakove SUP in Jagodina in order to get a driver's licence, and you said: "I would like to make a statement when on," and you give the date of the 21st of June, 1998, "with my family," and you then go on to describe the events that took place in June of 1998. Now, in this statement you've given the 21st of June, you told the Tribunal here that, in fact, it was the 13th of June. Can you explain that mistake?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not too far back in time. I don't think giving the wrong date is a big problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you have any documents with you when you -- to help you recall events when you were making this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm just going to take you to a number of particular passages in it. At the very last line on the page of translation that we have in front of us, you said -- describing the UCK roadblock, you said: "There were 20 Albanian persons in front of me, both sides in camouflage uniforms, some of them had black uniforms and I know the time was exactly 1300 hours." You recall saying that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I said that. I'm not very sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Again, you may not think it makes much difference, but you told the investigators of this Tribunal back in 2002 that there were ten persons, ten Albanian persons; it's now 20. Were you trying to exaggerate or had you just forgotten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said here that there were ten, but there were more than that. I gave them the minimum number. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, it's perhaps not a hugely important matter, but it's a matter that does require some clarification. I think if the previous statement of the witness is to be put to him, it's -- the correct statement should be put to him. In that November 2002 statement he said "approximately ten," not ten precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm grateful, and that is a correct statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You told the authorities in Serbia that there were 20. Do you think it may have been more than 20?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was surrounded by KLA when I was in the car. I don't know whether there were more than 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How were you able to give the time as being exactly 1300 hours, 1.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was around that time. It's been nine years now. I cannot tell you exactly, so I can say more things or less things now because it's been nine years. It's not that this happened a week ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Witness, I'm sure everybody understands that. What I'm trying to find out is how you were able to tell the SUP authorities just a year ago that the time was exactly 1300 hours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you gave your statement to the SUP authorities, you used the name -- the full name Nenad Remistar as the traffic policeman who was stopped by the KLA. Did you know his full name at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, how come his full name is put into that statement? Was that done by the SUP authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They knew his last name; I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, were they telling you what to put into the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, they simply marked down his last name. I only knew him by his first name of Nenad. They wrote his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did they tell you anything else about him, apart from his last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: A little later on in your statement, after you have described being kept in that room for two months, you said this: "I later found out that while I was in prison two brothers were in charge. One of them was called Lahi Brahimaj, nickname Maxhupi, and the other brother is called Nazmi Brahimaj. They are both from Jablanica village." When you said that you later found that out, what did you mean by that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was imprisoned and for four weeks I didn't know the name of anyone. Only after I was released, I saw their pictures and found out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Where was it you saw their pictures, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw their -- not their pictures, but their faces. They came there every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No. I'm going to read your last answer back to you, sir, and I'm going to ask you the same question. Your answer was: "I was imprisoned and for four weeks I didn't know the name of anyone. Only after I was released, I saw their pictures and found out." I ask you again, sir: Where was it after you were released that you saw their pictures and found out their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the two weeks I had more freedom, then I saw their faces and heard their names, but I didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: On Friday in answer to Mr. Di Fazio you said this --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't have the corrected in front of me. This is at page 33 of the transcript that we had on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: "After I was released, I wanted to find out their names. I knew them by appearance." Again, sir, it's right, isn't it, that after you were released, still up until that time you still didn't know the names of the people that you have now given the names to this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that, their names, yes, but I said -- I didn't say everything I knew in my statement there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm going to suggest to you -- well, first of all, let's go back. When was it that you were shown for the first time you were shown their pictures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't shown any pictures of them; I saw them in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Sir, are you trying to be truthful in your answers to this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm going back to an answer you gave just a little while ago. "I was imprisoned and for four weeks I didn't know the name of anyone. Only after I was released, I saw their pictures and found out." For the third time, sir, I ask you: When was it and where was it that you were shown their pictures and found out their names?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, you now for the second time say: "You were shown pictures," where the witness testified that he saw pictures; that is not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I appreciate there may be a subtle difference there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And especially since it comes down to details here. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You heard the Presiding Judge's point there, that you said that you saw their pictures and found out their names. Where did you see their pictures and how did you find out their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any pictures of them. I saw their faces every day, and I learned their names, hearing someone speaking of or to them by that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Let me suggest this to you, sir: When you were released from Jablanica and you were told that you were free to go, you went straight to State Security headquarters in Djakovica, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What year are you talking?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, what year were you released from Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 25th, 1988.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The answer was translated as 1988. You must mean 1998, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: That's what the witness said: "1988."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I wasn't arguing with the translation; I'm asking the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you mean 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And when you left Jablanica, the first thing you did was you went straight to the State Security headquarters in Djakovica, didn't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I went after five days to get some papers, driving licence, the ID. I went there to get a copy of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Let's go back to the statement that you gave in 2006 in Jagodina. In that statement you told them this. Please listen carefully: "When I was released from detention, I went to report the case to the chief of State Security Camovic. From Jablanica I walked. Along the way I saw some Romas who were travelling with horse-drawn cart, but from Djakovica until I arrived at Camovic I didn't talk to anyone about it. The Romas gave me a lift from Grgoc to Crmljane, and from there I went to Djakovica on foot and reported the case to Camovic." I'm going to break that down in stages, sir. Do you agree with me that what has been written down in Jagodina last year is that you told the SUP authorities there that you left Jablanica, you walked, you got a lift on a horse-drawn cart for part of the way, and then you walked again until you got to Djakovica and reported the case to Camovic, all on the same day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They have written it wrongly. I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So you say that you waited for five days, is that it, before going to the State Security headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I went to the doctor. I wanted to get better, and then I went to get those papers. They have written what they wanted. I didn't state what you are putting to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: At the very end of the statement, sir, the one that you gave in 2006 in Jagodina, are these words: "Official Note was read over to the citizen pursuant to Article 226, paragraph 5, of the ZKP, and he has no objections." When this statement was finished, did they read it over to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you read it yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know how to read Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you also put your finger-print on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And when you signed it and put your finger-print on it, did you appreciate that you were saying that the contents of the statement were true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know what they had written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you didn't ask them to read it over to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And when they wrote that they had read it over to you, that was a lie, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Is the -- or going back to 1998 now. Was the DB, the State Security, responsible for issuing driver's licences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In 1998, the year that you had been in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there after five days to get my papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you hear my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Let's try again. Going back to 1998 now, was the DB, the State Security, responsible for issuing driver's licences in Gjakove?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That wasn't the responsibility of SUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were together in the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, but the chief of State Security doesn't issue driver's licences or he didn't issue driver's licences in 1998, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. His employees were those who issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, you told -- again back in 2006, you told the authorities in Jagodina that you reported to Camovic about what had happened to you in Jablanica; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they have added that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, let's understand this. You knew Camovic by his first name of Streok; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sret.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I apologise, Sret. Thank you. And you had known him for a period of some 20 years back in 1998; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because he was a professor in the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And did you used to see him regularly during those 20 years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not for some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In relation to July of 1998, when was the last time before that that you had seen Sret?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came out of Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And before you came out of Jablanica, when was the last time you had seen him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It was a long time. It's a long time. I don't know now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you -- do you agree, let's deal with that, first of all, do you agree that you did go to see him in July of 1998 after you came out of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him in a coffee place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Pashtrik Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And why did you go to meet him in the Pashtrik Hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where I found him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And what did you say to him when you found him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. He asked me, How was it in Jabllanice? I told him that they took away my papers, and then he told me, Come tomorrow, bring the necessary documents, and you will get a copy of new papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm just going to read that part of that answer back to you. I asked you: "What did you say to him when you found him?" You answered: "Nothing. He asked me, How was it in Jabllanice?" Did it appear to you, sir, that he already knew that you had been in Jablanica when you came in to see him in the coffee shop in the Hotel Pashtrik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, there's -- the way the questions are being framed and the flow of the answers may give rise to -- well, I don't know what it may give rise to, but there's a possibility -- there's a lack of clarity concerning whether this was a chance meeting or an arranged meeting. That can be clarified with a single question. I rather gathered -- well, I rather won't say -- but it's not clear from --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I will deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It seems that Mr. Harvey takes your point, Mr. Di Fazio. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Before I get to that specific question, I would like an answer to this question, sir: By the time you saw Mr. Camovic in the Hotel Pashtrik, did it seem to you that he already knew -- from what he said to you, did it appear that he already knew that you had been in Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he knew it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And did he know that because you had told somebody else in the State Security already or did he know from other reasons, as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you met Camovic, did you -- had you gone to the Hotel Pashtrik because you knew that was where you were likely to find him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I just went there to have a coffee, and then I met him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, had you gone to Djakovica that day in order to get your driver's licence and other documents sorted out or had you just gone there for coffee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Pashtrik to have a coffee, and I had my papers in the Gjakove SUP, but this is far from Pashtrik. It's not in the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Had you already been to the Gjakove SUP by the time you went to the Hotel Pashtrik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Okay. So you went first to the Hotel Pashtrik. Did you go there expecting or hoping to see Mr. Camovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I just went there to have a coffee and ran into him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Were you on your own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Was Mr. Camovic on his own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was with some three friends of his whom I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did he call you over or did you go over to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went over to him because I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you sit down and have coffee with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found them there and we had the coffee together. And then I stayed there for half an hour and left, leaving them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So you talked with him for half an hour about your experiences in Jablanica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't talk with him for half an hour, but for some ten minutes. He asked me how it was, what did you go through? And I said it was a very bad time. The KLA was harsh on me. I told him that I was maltreated, then they took away my car. And then he told me, Bring your photos and you will have a duplicate of the papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And did you go in to see him the next day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you see him again to discuss this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't meet him anymore. I took the photos, handed them there, and after two days they gave me the papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you see a police officer or a state security office by the name of Pavle Zuvic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was to see the doctor, then on the way back from the doctor he was a reservist policeman and I met him. And he asked me, How was it? Did you see Nenad? I said, Yes. We were together for one night, tied up and tortured, and then after that I didn't see him. This is all I talked with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And where was it that you saw Pavle Zuvic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the outpatient clinic in the textile factory when I just left the clinic; some 200 metres away from it I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Was he on duty or was he just -- this is just a chance meeting in the street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in a civilian car. He was in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Have you ever been a reservist policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had a very large family of 40 members. I didn't have time to serve as policeman. I was at home. I had to work hard to keep the family.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you were having your conversation with Sret Camovic, which language were you speaking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did he appear interested in who was responsible for your torture in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't ask me, even though he knew the place better than I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How do you know that he knew the place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he knew every detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He knew the names better than I did, the names of the persons that I saw there during the imprisonment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So he was the person who told you their names, was he? MR. DI FAZIO: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no -- MR. DI FAZIO: -- wasn't what the witness said at all --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was a question of Mr. Harvey. He suggested something in a very leading way which -- MR. DI FAZIO: Well that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- as far as I understand is not -- MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps I misunderstood. I thought that Mr. Harvey was concluding that from the answer that was being given. If it's a suggestion, I have no problem with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you can put the question again to the witness, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And so Sret Camovic knew the names better than you did, the names of the persons that you saw there during your imprisonment. That's your evidence; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He knew the terrain because I didn't ask him names or surnames. He knew everything that was going on in the Gjakove municipality. He knew every house, every family. He's older than me. He knew everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. He knew the names better than you did; that's what you just told us, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Pardon, Mr. Harvey, may I interrupt. Are we now speaking of Sret Camovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 6, one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Are we speaking of Pavle Zuvic or again of Sret Camovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry if I've created confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I am speaking of Sret Camovic, and you said -- if I understand your answer correctly, you said that Sret Camovic knew the names better than you did. Isn't that what you told us, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said he knew the terrain, he worked in the Gjakove municipality. I am a villager myself. I did not know everybody. He knew all the villages and -- in the commune or in the municipality of Gjakove better than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, Witness, we have your answers in front of you. I'm not going to argue with you. It's right, isn't it, that Sret Camovic knew names of people in Jablanica and he told you that he knew those names, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, as head of State Security, was he -- did he ask you anything at all about the people who tortured you, as you have told us, in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: He wasn't interested to get information on their behaviour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And he never asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, I'd like to have one matter explored a bit more in detail. Witness 6, about Sret Camovic knowing people, you said only one or two minutes ago, and I think you were talking about him, you said: "He knew the names better than I did, the names of the persons that I saw there during the imprisonment." What did you exactly mean when you said that? Because later your answer suggests that he would not know the names of those persons. Could you tell us what you meant when you gave that first answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was the chief and knew the region of Gjakove. I did not say that he knew every name or surname. He knew the terrain. He knew the families, who came from which family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But when you spoke with him, did he appear to know who the persons were that you saw during your imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. He did not ask me about them at all. Whether he knew them or didn't know them, I don't know, because he did not ask me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You see, Witness, you have told this Tribunal about a number of people who were in Jablanica with you who were being systematically tortured, and you have mentioned Nenad, a police officer; you have mentioned a Bosnian who worked for Elektro in Decani; you have mentioned three Montenegrins; you have mentioned an Albanian Muslim who was fat, in his 40s, who was delivered in the trunk of a Mercedes and who came from Zahaq; you have mentioned Pal Krasniqi; you have mentioned another man, a Catholic Albanian from Grabanica. Now, are you saying, sir, that Sret Camovic knew everything about all of those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, he didn't ask me. And this person from Grabanica is not a Catholic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, we'll come back to that. But what I'm trying to understand, sir, is how you could be talking with the head of State Security and he's not remotely interested in all of these people who you say were tortured in Jabllanice. Now, did you tell him that you saw anybody else being tortured there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. He didn't ask me about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you didn't think it was important to tell him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was important, but the situation was such that I did not tell him anything and he did not ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And was it the same day or some other day when you went to get your driving licence sorted out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two days later I went for the papers. I took the photos to the place and I got the driving licence and the ID card.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And did you see any officers of the State Security when you went there for your driver's licence and ID card?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. These were only women that were working in those offices. There were no officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you attempt to speak to anybody from State Security when you went there two days later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So, despite everything that had been done to you and everything that you say had been done to all of these other people, the only thing that you were interested in doing was renewing your driver's licence. Do we understand you correctly, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The war started and I did not have time to tell them anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: What do you mean, the war started and you didn't have time to tell them anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you now, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You had time to sit and have coffee for half an hour with Mr. Camovic. You had time to go back two days later to renew your driver's licence. You had time to go to the doctor. You had time to talk with Pavle Zuvic. What do you mean the war started and you didn't have time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they did not ask me how you were and where you were, I did not give them any answers. And then I had to give that other statement that you saw later, when I went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Which was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness said that he had a conversation for ten minutes with Mr. Camovic. He went there for half an hour but had a conversation, ten minutes; page 21, line 9. And apart from that, I wonder whether it's fully appropriate to put to the witness: You found time to go and see the doctor, which is -- might be -- he might have been moved by other reasons. So therefore, precision there is the first thing required; and second, to say: You found time to drink coffee, you found time to see the doctor suggests more or less that these are similar things, which they certainly are not. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I certainly don't mean to minimise or trivialise any of these matters. I'm responding, though, of course, to the witness's answer that: "The war started and I did not have time to tell them anything." I merely seek to point out that over a period of days he was not prevented by whatever he means by the war starting; he was not prevented from doing other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: May I, Witness, just put this to you. You have never given to the Serb authorities the stories concerning other individuals who were in Jablanica with you, with the exception of Nenad Remistar. Isn't that correct? You've never given that information to the Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked me about him and I told them about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you say "they," who are you talking about at this point, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Jagodine, when they asked me questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You also told an investigator for the Office of the Prosecutor -- you know Pekka Haverinen, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I don't know. There were many and I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, do you recall that you were interviewed on the 17th and the 18th of January, 2003, and let me just put this aspect of your statement to you, it's very brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm looking at the statement of the 18th of -- 17th/18th of January, on the second page of that statement on the fourth unnumbered paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You said this: "After I was released, I heard from a Serb police that Nenad had been killed but his body was not dumped in the lake of Radoniq as many others, but maybe somewhere up in the mountains in the area surrounding Peje or Kline." First of all, sir, do you remember saying that to an investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Who was the Serb police officer who gave you this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pavle.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And when do you say he gave you that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The day that I went to the doctor and I was coming out of the clinic and I met him for three or four minutes [as interpreted] on the street. That's what he told me on that occasion. Whether he was taken to the lake or to the mountain, I mean his body, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm trying to understand the statement that you gave to Mr. Haverinen. The date when you went to the doctor we know from the doctor's statement was the 30th of July, 1998, five days after you left Jabllanice. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you told Mr. Haverinen on the 18th of January, 2003, that Pavle Zuvic had told you that "Nenad had been killed but his body was not dumped in the lake of Radoniq as many others." Do you agree that you made that statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have said that, but maybe also the translators have gotten it wrong. I don't know about it. There are mistakes in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, we may have to ask you to look at the original of that, sir. Have you -- have you reviewed your original statement in Albanian to that interpreter -- to that investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it until later, when I saw it myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I cannot for the full hundred per cent exclude that there's some confusion. Witness 6, your statement given in January 2003 doesn't say that you know anything about where the -- where the body of Nenad was dumped, but in that statement we only find that you heard from a Serb policeman that the body was not dumped at Lake Radonjic but maybe somewhere else. Is that what you heard from this policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is it true that you had no personal knowledge of where the body was dumped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not so much concerned with whether you know where the body was dumped. I just want this to be clear, that in your conversation with Pavle Zuvic on the 30th of July, 1998, he told you that Nenad's body was not dumped in the lake of Radoniq, as many others. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he told me and I don't know any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: After you went to the doctor on the 30th of July, 1998, you never had any further conversation with anybody in the Serb police or in the Serb State Security about your experiences in Jablanica; is that correct sir? That's, of course, up until 2006.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I had no contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you ever give a statement to the International Committee of the Red Cross concerning the disappearance of Nenad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked me questions and I gave them answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you recall when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Can you recall whether it was a short time after you left Jabllanice or many years later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you spoke with representatives of the International Committee for the Red Cross, was that, shall we say, within six months to a year or many years later after you left Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was 2002 or 2003 when I started to give my statements to the internationals.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Going back, sir, to your statement to Zoran Nikic in Jagodina, you are quoted there as saying: "I have reported this case about me and policeman Remistar to the ICTY investigators in Prizren in 2000 and 2001 in Pristina." Are those dates accurate, sir, or is that a mistake?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember what year it was, but I know that it was in Prizren, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you're also reported as having told Zoran Nikic in Jagodina: "I don't know any other names, apart from the two brothers I have mentioned above," and that, of course, would be Lahi Brahimaj and Nazmi Brahimaj, "nor have I been able to find out anything but I would like to know their names. I know that one of them is in The Hague now." Do you recall making that statement, that you didn't know any other names apart from those two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question was about those two.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You were unable to give any other names, apart from those two, back in 2006. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only those two.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You didn't, for instance, remember the name of Hamza Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't remember it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you didn't remember the name of Gani Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't remember his name either. I couldn't remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to assist us, if you would, please, in trying to understand how many people were with you in Jabllanice at different stages during the six weeks that you have told us that you were there. First of all, you arrived in Jabllanice on the afternoon of the 13th of June. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And if you were stopped at or around 1.00 in the afternoon and you were held, as you've told us, for something like two hours at the road side; that would take us to around about 3.00. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe later, 3.30, 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you then drove through a series of villages until your wife and children were dropped off, and then you continued on to Jabllanice. Was it dark by the time you got to Jabllanice or was it still light, bearing in mind that this is July [sic]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was light.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Are we talking approximately 6.00 in the evening or later or earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you have told this Tribunal that you and Nenad were taken to the building immediately on the left inside the gate when you arrived at Jabllanice. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you were kept in that building overnight. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And sometime the next day you were taken to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you were put in the room on the left-hand side of the entrance door to the house, at the front. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So at this stage we have you and Nenad together in that room; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Was Nenad in a different room from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They took him away. They took me to that room and I don't know where they took him to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I see. So you were on your own in that room and you don't know where he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you -- sorry. Did you see him again after you were taken to that room? Did you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you see Nenad again after you were taken to that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I heard the witness say "jo," meaning no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just before Mr. Harvey continues, I notice the time. There's one very brief matter I would like to raise with Your Honours in the absence of the witness. It might take a second or two, and I wonder, if that's a convenient, moment we might break at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, when --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: This is as convenient a moment as any other, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, we can't ask the witness to leave the courtroom unless we have all the curtains down. That --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The quickest way of doing it would be for the witness to remove his earphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that would be enough. Could you take off -- Witness 6, could you take off your earphones for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's just a very minor point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just wanted to make sure that my understanding on this was correct in the light of some of the questions and the answers. So far as we are aware, at least, there is no direct evidence of the death of Nenad Remistar in this case, and I simply thought that some of the questions and answers that proceeded, or seem to be proceeding on the assumption that there might be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm certainly happy to clarify any misapprehension that there may be. I'm also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether there's any direct evidence or whether there will be any direct evidence, because the Chamber doesn't know, but at least this witness, when he spoke, I think about the death of Nenad Remistar, it was always hearsay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes, well, it was -- in the light of that and in the way that the questions were asked and answered that I simply wanted to have the position clarified, because of course we have all seen the evidence on which the Prosecution has brought the indictment, some of which, of course, Your Honours haven't seen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and therefore, the comment that I make is based upon not just to review the evidence that has been called but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But also on what you expect will be presented.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- what we think the evidence will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: May I just respond briefly, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I want to make it absolutely clear that we have absolutely no information to suggest that Nenad Remistar is dead or died by foul means, and I certainly didn't wish any of my questions to be taken as an acknowledgement or admission of that. I'm merely dealing with the witness's third-hand hearsay understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. So therefore, where you said we have absolutely no information to suggest, that might be a bit too strong because we have the testimony of this witness who says that he heard about it. So therefore -- but we all agree that that's hearsay until now and whether it's second- or third-hand hearsay depends on what the source knew or --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's perhaps not fully explored. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I simply meant, raise the issue for clarification for Your Honours; not necessarily for clarification with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then this was the point you would like to raise? Then we'll have a break and we'll resume at -- but let's first ask the witness to put his earphones on again. Witness 6, there was a procedural matter we had to discuss, but we now take our time for a break. We'll resume at 11.00, and could Mr. Harvey give us any indication on how much time he would still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It will certainly be all of the next session, Your Honour. I cannot with certainty rule out the possibility that I won't go over into the third session, but I will certainly finish with this witness today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but there are other Defence counsel as well. Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I would expect something in the region of 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 40 minutes. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: 15 minutes to a half-hour. MR. DI FAZIO: Thus far, very little re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thus far. MR. DI FAZIO: A matter of minutes at the absolute most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I will be more than happy to keep the Chamber updated as the questioning progresses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Likewise. It may well be that some of the questions that I had in mind may will have already been asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Just a logistical matter, if Your Honours please, can we - the Prosecution, that is - safely say or rely on the assumption that we don't need the next witness brought here until at least the completion of the next session. I see Defence counsel nodding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and at the same time hearing -- you said next session certainly, then perhaps even a bit more. The Chamber would very much like not to -- that not the whole of today's time will be spent on this witness. So therefore, try to see whether we can start with the next witness. I'm not thinking of -- of an hour, but rather at least that we would have a start half an hour for the next witness. Here, of course, we -- the evidence in chief was elicited in a non-leading way, so therefore that the balance between Prosecution and Defence there is always a bit different. Let's -- the parties are urged to find the most efficient way, and -- no, let me not further comment on this at this moment. We'll have a break and we'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, might I very, very briefly introduce a new colleague who's joined the Prosecution, Ms. Antoinette Issa. She will be leading the next witness, and I just wanted to inform the Trial Chamber of this new face that you see before you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Di Fazio. And welcome in court, Ms. Issa. Mr. Harvey, are you ready to --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: On behalf of the Defence, we welcome Ms. Issa as well. Your Honour, two very quick corrections, if I may. I did misstate myself at page 33 when I put to the witness that we were talking about the month of July when he was first taken to Jabllanice. Of course, it should have been June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I think that's clear to everybody. There was also a point on page 29 when the witness was asked how long he spoke with Pavle Zuvic when he met him in the street. My -- I'm told that the transcript reads - we're having some problems with our technology over here - but I'm told that the transcript reads three to four minutes, but in fact what the witness had said was ten minutes. It's not a major point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that at least it was translated as three to four minutes, but I'm just looking now at page --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: 29, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- 29. Let me just -- yes, it's line 20. Witness 6, you told us that you met Pavle when you were coming out of the clinic. There was some confusion about how long you then saw him. Could you tell us how long that was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't look at the time. We were just standing and talking. I can't tell you exactly, five or ten minutes, maybe, but the important thing is that we talked together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You briefly met in passing and had a conversation which lasted for at least a couple of minutes. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can't be very precise about the minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: More important is, obviously, what was said, Witness 6, and you have told us that during that conversation Pavle Zuvic told you that he believed that Nenad Remistar had been killed at Jabllanice. That's right, that's what he told you, yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: He didn't tell you how he knew that or who told him that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me, and I didn't ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: He told you that the body was not dumped near Radoniq canal; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: He didn't tell you that the body was not dumped near the canal -- in Lake Radoniq, sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did he tell you that he thought that it was dumped somewhere in the mountains near Peje or Klina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what he told me. He was buried on the side of the street -- of a street, but I don't know the place where.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And he didn't tell you what his source of information was about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And he didn't tell you -- sorry. And he didn't tell you whether that was merely a rumour or something that he had discovered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he got that information from.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, to come back to your time in Jabllanice and who was with you, when you were in the room that you have described in the house, at what time do you say you were taken to that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was afternoon. It was still daylight.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, you understand what I mean by the room in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And that is different from the first building that you were taken to on your first night. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the room which is situated once you enter the yard on the left side. We stayed there all night, and we were beaten and tortured and we had lost consciousness, me and Nenad. I don't know what time it was when they took us to another room, again on the left side of a room -- of a building with four rooms, and then I don't know what happened to Nenad after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It may be something to do with the translation but what's just come up on my screen was that you said: "I don't know what time it was when they took us to another room, again on the left side of a building with four rooms, and then I don't know what happened to Nenad after that." Did they take you both to this other room on the left-hand side of the building with four rooms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only myself. He was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And this was after 24 hours; is that your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you then stayed alone in that room for - was it - two weeks --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- three weeks, three and a half weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two weeks, I think, approximately two weeks. I don't know exactly. I couldn't tell day from night because I was shut in the room and I wasn't able to know what time it was, whether it was day-time or night-time. I was locked up and beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: This is a room that has a window, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And what do you mean by saying you couldn't tell whether it was day or night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was barred from -- with some planks, wooden planks. It was boarded with some wooden planks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And is your testimony that you never left that room for any purpose at all during those two weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Does that mean no, you didn't leave the room, or no, you are not saying you didn't leave the room? Let me put the question more clearly. Were you ever taken out of that room during those two weeks, for example, to go to the toilet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once a week, because I wasn't given anything to eat so I couldn't -- I didn't need to go more often.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Who took you out of the room to take you to the toilet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some persons there, unknown persons to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Are you being entirely truthful when you say that you were only taken out once a week to go to the toilet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go out more often because, as I said, I didn't have anything to eat or to drink. I was sick. I often was unconscious.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You would agree, wouldn't you, that even if the window was boarded up, it would still be possible to see light through the cracks; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could see a little light, but there was another cover, so to say, I don't know, maybe kind of garage which prevented you from seeing clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm just trying to deal with your statement that: "I couldn't tell day from night," and I'm trying to explore with you whether you are so upset about your experience that you are exaggerating or whether you're lying to this Tribunal. Are you saying that you could not tell whether it was light outside at any time during that period of two weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could see some light from a crack but not much to speak of.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you have a watch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, but they took it away from me. They took away my watch and my underpants. I was almost naked. My T-shirt and my trousers were torn. They took away my watch -- or better say, they stole it from me and returned it to me after four weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Oh, so they did give it back to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And are you saying that you were never given a drop of water in two weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They brought us very little water in those glass jars, but not in a proper glass. And I don't know where they fetched the water from. The water was very dirty.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] You just said: "They brought us very little water ..." My understanding, Witness, is that during those two weeks you were entirely on your own in that room. Am I wrong about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Myself. I mean myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And, Witness, I'm looking at your first statement to the ICTY investigator that you made in November of 2002, page 5 of the last paragraph of that statement, we read this: "During my detention period I got a piece of bread every day and water to drink." I'm not suggesting, Witness, that that was an ideal diet, but is it right that you got a piece of bread every day and water to drink?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They brought, but I wasn't able to eat or to drink anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You also indicated when you gave your statement to Zoran Nikic last year: "Occasionally they gave me salami, bread, beans." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, you say "no." They never gave you salami or beans?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Can you think of any reason why the SUP officer to whom you gave that statement last year would suddenly just put that in your statement if it never happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they've written there. I gave less details. I don't know what they have written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Or isn't the truth of it this: That you are exaggerating and distorting what exactly happened in Jabllanice before this Tribunal because you want to hurt my client, Lahi Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm telling you, sir, is true. What are you asking me about, I don't know, because those persons kidnapped me and did to me what they did. And this is true, but, however, nine years have passed by since that time, and things may be put rather differently sometimes. But the persons who are there are alive and that's why I'm here to testify against them. I'm not here to tell you whether I eat or not eat or beans or bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Sir, the only --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, if you don't remember something, just tell us. Nevertheless, you are here to answer all questions put to you. And therefore, the issue now is: Did you get anything to eat and to drink and what did you get to eat and to drink. That is what Mr. Harvey wants to find out, and he has put to you that at another occasion you have given information which was not exactly the same as you gave today; that is, once you talked about getting some bread and water every day, at another moment it's put on paper that you would have said that you got some salami or beans. Now, tell us, it was a period of six weeks, approximately. Was the food in the beginning and the water the same as later? Were there any changes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They gave us a piece of bread and some marmalade. When I felt a little better to eat and to drink, in the last two weeks it happened that we ate bread and beans. I was with Gani Brahimaj; we were together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, I'll come on to that in a little while. What I was trying to do with your assistance, Witness 6, was to establish how long you remained alone in that room after Nenad was taken away and before the Bosnian and three Montenegrins arrived. Do you recall how long a time that was, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And how did you find out that the Bosnian worked at Elektro in Decani? Did you discuss that with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The soldiers told him, You have worked for Serbia in Elektrokosova. I didn't speak with him about that because he spoke almost no Albanian.
