utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I think you told us that he did speak some Albanian and you did have some conversation. Was that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he talked, but I didn't understand him because he kept mixing up Albanian with Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You also told us that the three Montenegrins, you didn't know them from before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Does that mean that you actually did know the Bosnian from before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you ever find out any of their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How many days and nights were you together in the same room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three or four days, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you ever tell any of them your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And after three or four days, were they taken away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were taken away and they were not brought there anymore. I don't know where they were taken to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: But for those three or four days, you all stayed together the entire time, 24 hours a day, in that room. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And during that time you have said that they were beaten and pierced with knives all over their bodies. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And who was present when that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How many people were involved in that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One person had the knife. They came one by one. Someone kicked him with blows, someone gave slaps to him, someone used baseball bats.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Can you describe the people who did this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't describe them to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I suggest that's because it never happened. You never saw it; it never happened, and you're just making this up, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not making it up. Things are as I described them, but these persons I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: All of them were pierced with knives, the Bosnian and the three Montenegrins? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bosnian had more of them; the others less.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you were there the entire time, but nobody pierced you with knives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Because, of course, if they had pierced you with knives we would be able to see your scars, wouldn't we?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can show you the wound I have that was caused to me by a baseball bat. I am here. I can show you my wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: We'll come to that. After three or four days, the Bosnian, the three Montenegrins were taken away. And then you told us at some time after that an Albanian Muslim who you describe as fat and in his 40s who came from Zahaq was brought in the trunk of a Mercedes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he was apprehended. He was from Zahaq and, as I said, they brought him in the trunk of his own car. And this was before I was released, a week or two before I was released, and I had more freedom to move around and I saw it when they got him out of the trunk.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So this is in the last two weeks of your presence in Jabllanice. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, about four weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I want to make sure that we understand each other. You're saying that it's about four weeks before you were released or four weeks after you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four weeks after I arrived. At that time I had a little more freedom to go out into the yard, and I saw what happened myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you see the Mercedes arrive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you see him get out of the trunk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And did -- was he put in the same room in which you were staying, that's the front room on the left of the entrance door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was in the right-hand side room. He was in another room.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you have conversation with him while he was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: From whom did you learn that he was from Zahaq?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had spoken to Pal Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How many days in all did the man from Zahaq stay at Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When he arrived, could you see what condition he was in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Was he able to stand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was lying down on the floor in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry to interrupt. I'm just looking at page 49, line 21, where the witness's answer as translated in response to the question: "From whom did you learn that he was from Zahaq?" is recorded as: "I had spoken to Pal Krasniqi." And for the sake of clarification, when the words "had spoken" appear, it would certainly assist my understanding of this witness's testimony to know whether he is there referring to a conversation which had taken place before this man from Zahaq arrived; in other words, had spoken before then, or he means had spoken subsequently to Pal Krasniqi because of certain answers he's given already.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I can assure my learned friend that I have no intention of leaving it there. I do intend to come back to it, but I want to take my course with this witness, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you said that he was not able to stand, the man from Zahaq, he was lying down in the room on the other side of the front door. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes I was ordered to give him some water to drink.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And at that stage, were you working in the kitchens?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So this is before you started to work in the kitchens that he was brought to Jabllanice. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was during those days that I had a little more freedom when he was brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Just so that we understand the sequence, you were kept, you say, for approximately four weeks before you were allowed some freedom. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After four weeks, I was a little more free to move.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And then was there a time when you were a little more free to move and then a later time when you worked in the kitchens?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not work in the kitchen. I just washed up the dishes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, some of us might call that work. I'll come back to that. When you said the man from Zahaq was only there for two days, was anybody else brought in during the time when he was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How many other people were brought in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pal Krasniqi and the one from Grabanica. I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And were they brought in together, Pal and the one from Grabanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Who --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. At different times.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Who came first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And did Pal arrive before the man from Zahaq or after?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person from Zahaq came earlier, one day earlier, so one day before Pal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And the man from Grabanice, when did he come in relation to Pal and the man from Zahaq?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About two or three hours later; I saw him when they brought him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Two or three hours later than Pal or two or three hours later than the man from Zahaq?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Pal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, you knew Pal from before, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How did you learn his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I took bread and water to him, I asked him what his name was and where he was from.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And was he in the same room as the man from Zahaq?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, both of them were beaten up, Pal and the one from Zahaq. The one from Zahaq was beaten up also the day before, and the second day they were both beaten continuously.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you say "continuously," was there a soldier or more than one soldier with them the entire day, on that second day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes there was one at the door, sometimes they did not beat them. But the soldiers would go one after the other, and they beat them; that was their programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Again, I'd like to understand that. You say: "Sometimes there was one at the door, sometimes they did not beat them." But the soldiers would go one after another. Does that mean there was always a soldier at -- standing guard at the door or somebody, a soldier, in there beating them? And let me give you the third opportunity, the third option, that there was no one there -- that there were times when there was no soldier with them at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were times when there was no soldier there and the door was locked. There was such occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And what about the man from Grabanice, where was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the same room as Pal and the one from Zahaq.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And was the man from Grabanice beaten as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he was married to someone from Jabllanice, and his wife's family came and intervened and he was not beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So he arrived on the second day when the man from Zahaq was there, and although they beat Pal, they didn't touch the man from Grabanice; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you went into that room and saw what condition the man from Zahaq was in; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only when I took him some water to drink, I could see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Was he able to drink the water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had to give it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you gave it to him, did he drink it with your assistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes I left the water there, in the jar in the room, and Pal Krasniqi helped him to drink it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you say "sometimes," that suggests that you went on more than one occasion, certainly, to see him in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only the times when I had to give him the water or the bread, because I was not in their room. I went up to the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you went into the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You told us a moment ago -- when I asked you, "Was he able to drink the water?", you answered, "No, I had to give it to him." Now, did you give him the water or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left the water inside the room, close to the door, and Pal would take it. And whether they drank it or whether he drank it or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: What can you tell us about the physical condition of the man from Zahaq? Was he lying down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, lying down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Were his eyes open?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Closed. He was fat and also swollen because of the beating, so his eyes -- he could not open his eyes. He was all swollen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: What part did you see swollen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please. Well, physically he was fat and because of the beating, I could not -- I thought that his clothes could not contain his body because of the swelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you actually see him being beaten at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when they got him off the trunk of the car, they beat him at that time. Nazmi, Lahi, and the persons that I have already stated in my statement. And after that, when he attempted to escape, he was caught, the person from Zahaq and Pal Krasniqi, they were caught. It was the other one from Grabanice who opened the window and escaped from the window. He was not beaten, so he could escape, he could run, while the two others who were beaten, they could not run at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, you you've just told us - and I'll be corrected if I'm wrong - you've just told us for the first time that he was beaten by Nazmi, Lahi, and the persons that I have already stated in my statement. First of all, I put it to you that Lahi was not present when this individual was brought to Jabllanice and that you are, at best, mistaken about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And I'm looking at your statement - and again I'll be corrected if I'm wrong - but there is no reference in the statement where you first mention these individuals, when you first mentioned the man from Zahaq, and that is November of 2002. There's no mention of who did the beating. Do you think that you may have been mistaken about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not mistaken, but maybe the translator forgot to put it in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, in your second statement, which is the first time that you mention the attempted escape, you said this --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'm at page 3 of the statement, the 17th and 18th of January, 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- "now," that's the last paragraph on that page. "Now, I also remember that this Albanian," that's the Albanian from Zahaq, "tried to escape from the prison together with the two other prisoners." Is it right, sir, that you didn't remember anything about this supposed escape in your first statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Is it right that when you first gave a statement to the OTP investigator in November of 2002, you said nothing at all about an attempted escape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I forgot. I did not remember it to mention it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And again I'm looking at your second statement, the one in February of 2003. You said nothing about him being beaten when he arrived in the trunk of the car on that occasion, but I'll come to the question of Pal Krasniqi again, if I may. As Mr. Emmerson pointed out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I'm just trying to find the February 2003 -- MR. DI FAZIO: I think that's a mistake, if Your Honours please. I think it's just -- it's in fact quite -- unless -- it's January. It's January, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: January of 2003 or February of 2004, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I insist on precision, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Point taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Especially since you are going in so much detail the Chamber wonders whether that -- not to prevent you from going into details, but if you are asking about such details and at the same time are talking about working in the kitchens, where the testimony of the witness was, that he almost, at least in his later time, was with Gani, where he said Gani was a cook. Where he once mentioned a kitchen he was talking about a makeshift kitchen in which he was when the people escaped, or not to say: Was that when you worked in the kitchens is -- is -- well, especially since you insist so much on tiny little details and what was said, et cetera, that, to be very precise as well, and the Chamber wonders -- of course, it's -- it's good now and then to go into the depth and to test the evidence, but sometimes it takes a form which my fellow Judges and I consider not -- not very useful.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I accept that admonishment. I am trying as best I can using the materials we have, not all of which, of course, are within the statements of this witness, to test the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- extent to which he is both being accurate and -- and honest in his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we do understand. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm trying not to overdo the detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Witness, you did say that you had learned -- you had spoken with Pal Krasniqi and it was him -- from him that you had learned that this man came from Zahaq. Now, when did you have that conversation with Pal Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before two weeks -- I mean, two weeks before I was released and I was freer to move around. And you asked me about the kitchen. This was not a proper kitchen in a building like this one here. It was in the meadow. It was not a proper kitchen. It was in the meadow, and you could see around for several metres -- thousand metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Where was it that you had the conversation with Pal Krasniqi, where he told you that the man came from Zahaq?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the yard, when he was allowed to go into the yard as well. I asked him where the other person was from and he said, He's from Zahaq, and he didn't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Was that on Pal's first day or his second day there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was after some time when he was able to walk and get out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Was the man from Zahaq still there at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He had been sent to the hospital in Gllogjan of Decane. That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And from whom did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used to talk to Gani Brahimaj. He worked as a cook. He was close to me, and I spoke to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How far was Gani Brahimaj's house from the barracks where you were staying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 40 or 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you went to Gani Brahimaj's house, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: If you didn't go there, how did you know where it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Where was the bread baked for the soldiers in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the concrete wall is, the white concrete wall is; it used to be covered and there was an oven there, an iron oven, and that's where Gani baked the bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you helped him bake the bread, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, perhaps just for the witness. Witness 6, the sound you hear is a monthly testing of security devices in the Netherlands, so don't worry about what you hear. Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Not just for the witness, I'm grateful to hear that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Witness, how far away was Nazmi Brahimaj's house from the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know Jabllanice well. The day I left, I could see properly -- from the place I was in the prison, it could be of about 200, 250 metres far. When I went to get the papers and the car but they didn't give me the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So you went out to -- you went out of the barracks in order to get the papers from Nazmi Brahimaj. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you walked to his house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those documents that they gave me, that they had kept my car for military reasons, that was the last day. And it was that day that I found out where -- how far his house was from the detention place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How did you find his house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A soldier came with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How did you know where Gani's house was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That soldier told me, This is where his house and his office is, because I didn't know before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, of what house were you speaking? You were now referring to Gani's house again?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, his house --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Wasn't that addressed before?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The house where Gani Brahimaj lived, you knew where that was, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you were able to draw a sketch map for the investigator in 2002, November, showing the relationship between the barracks, the Gani Brahimaj house, and the Nazmi Brahimaj house, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They showed me on the computer and then I drew this sketch, indicating the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So you had a good recollection of the relationship between those buildings, even some three and a half years after you had left Jabllanice. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You had a good recollection of the relationship between those three buildings, the barracks, Gani's house, Nazmi's house over three years after you had left Jabllanice. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, could the witness first tell us what was shown to him on the computer before we ask further about recollections. Could you tell us, you said: "They showed me on the computer and then I drew this sketch indicating the distance." What exactly did they show you on the computer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The house where I was detained, that prison, and some other houses on a map. But now, if you ask me now, I don't know where these houses are, whether they are still there or destroyed or rebuilt, because I haven't been to Jabllanice ever since, so I don't know it very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did they show you pictures of these houses or did they show you a map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They showed -- they asked me to draw kind of sketch, to tell them how far these houses were from one another. They asked me, If you go to Jabllanice from Gjakove, I showed them which way to go. On the left side are the houses; the mosque is on the right side, a little bit further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But did they show you pictures of these houses as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. They showed me a picture of Jabllanice, of the entire Jabllanice village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And by a picture then, do you mean a map or a photograph, or an aerial photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A whole picture of the place called Jabllanice, no sketch. Only houses next to each other as they were, you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And was that picture taken from -- from the ground or was it taken from the air, for example, from an aeroplane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the air.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Sorry. Madam Registrar, perhaps if we could have 3D010062 on our screens, and then if we can go to the sketch map which should be on the 11th page of that exhibit -- of that document, rather. Looking at the top at U0031392, if we can scroll forward to that. Or perhaps, first of all, since we have this on the screen, I could ask the witness to identify it as his statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this as being a copy of the statement that you made on the 26th and 28th of November, 2002? You see your name there, you see the date at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember now because I have made many statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I don't know if we can scroll forward on this. No? MR. DI FAZIO: It's the 11th page onwards from the beginning of the document. I know that ERN numbers aren't supposed to be any guidance, but it's the -- 11 pages in, in to the statement.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: My apologies, but here are only ten pages in the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have at this moment -- in front of me, I have the original eight pages, and I have an English version which stops, Mr. Harvey, and therefore you refer to the ERN number, stops at -- MR. DI FAZIO: I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- last three digits, 391, whereas you wanted to take us to --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: 392, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I've got a note, if Your Honours please. I don't know if this is of assistance, I hope I'm not misleading anyone, but that this piece of evidence is 65 ter 777; now, that might be of some assistance, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm very grateful to Mr. Gramsci and we'll see if we can find that with the assistance of Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, it looks only -- as if all the attachments to the statement are not attached in the computer version. We could work, perhaps, to put the -- if we can't find an electronic version, then perhaps the sketch could be put on the ELMO so that the witness can look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That may be the quickest way of dealing with the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So I'm grateful to Your Honour for your assistance there. I have an unmarked copy of it. If that could be rotated anti-clockwise, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That -- this should not be shown to the public. I just -- because it bears ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour. Yes, thank you. And I understand from Ms. Trapani, in fact, we do have a -- a court number for this document. Just for reference's sake, it's 3D010193. I apologise; I didn't realise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Anyway, Witness, you see in front of you the sketch plan that you drew on the 28th of November, 2002, and you signed this document; didn't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And what does number 1 refer to on that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The place where I was detained for six weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you -- there is something written to the left of that that I can't read. Could you -- can you read that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the left?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes. On the left -- you've got a box with a 1 in it and then some writing, just to the left of that box, a word that begins with B by the look of it. What is that word?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's 3, not B. That box you are asking me is number 3. On the right side is the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Sir, I want you to look, if you would, please, at the left side of the drawing. You see a box with a number 1 in it, and then just above that the number 200. You see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, the box with the number 1 in it has some writing beside it just to the left. Can you tell us what that is? First of all, is it your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's "prison."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Okay. And then you have the number 200, and then above that another box with a 2 in it and what looks like Ibrahimaj beside that. Does that indicate 200 metres between buildings 1 and 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it's more than 200 metres or less, but approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Does the box in between the 1 and 2 indicate anything, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe that's the house of Gani Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And what does the number 3 indicate, sir, on the right-hand side of that drawing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And is that the word that you've written underneath there, the word for mosque?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, the mosque actually wasn't there during the war, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was there before the war. It was, but without a minaret. Now I don't know if they have repaired it because I haven't been to Jabllanice ever since. But when I entered there, when they took me to the prison, I saw it. And when I went to the Brahimajs' house to gather papers, I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The reality is, sir, that you were free to walk around that village almost the entire time you were in Jabllanice, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the two weeks that I mentioned that I had more freedom, I could have escaped but I didn't want to take that chance. I wanted to see what kind of people they were, what kind of integrity and morality they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You're saying you stayed out of curiosity when you could just have left? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, if Your Honours please, the witness actually said I didn't -- two things: I didn't want to take a chance, which carries with it various implications; and secondly, the other reason was he wanted to see what kind of people they were. So that it's twofold.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, similar things would have come into my mind, Mr. Di Fazio, when hearing the question because the suggestion that this is what the witness said is -- is certainly not -- doesn't reflect the whole of his answer. But let's hear what the witness says. Mr. Harvey asked you whether it was curiosity that kept you there, where you could have left the place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had the chance to leave but I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But Mr. Harvey asked you whether it was curiosity that made you stay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand very well the question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the last answer is -- is one: "I had the chance to leave, but I didn't." I am content with that answer and I'm willing to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to make my position clear to you in relation to the injuries that you say you received. I'm suggesting to you that you have exaggerated beyond all reason the stories of beatings, the stories of injuries, and the stories of the length of time that you were detained while you were being investigated at Jabllanice. You understand the suggestion that I am making to you, and I'm going to take you through this in a little bit of detail. But do you understand, first of all, that I am suggesting that you are exaggerating out of all reason and all reality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you what I experienced. You may say what you want, sir, but I'm telling you what I went through, the injuries and everything I suffered.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: First of all, you say that, on your arrival at Jabllanice, you were dragged out of the car and you were beaten repeatedly and beaten until they, the soldiers beating you, were exhausted. Do you stand by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They kept changing all the time. They took turns. I was unconscious because of the tortures.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You said they beat you with whatever they could lay their hands on, including baseball bats. You stand by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, I do. They used anything they could lay hold -- hands on, baseball bats, sticks, whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And this was all on the first night that you arrived there; correct? I'm just dealing with that first night for now. We'll come to the other stuff later.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the first night, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And did those beatings continue throughout the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They beat us continuously.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I just want to make sure that we all understand correctly. They beat you from your arrival throughout the night until dawn. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was unconscious. Sometimes I regained my consciousness, sometimes not, and I can't really tell you because you understand. When you are not aware of what happens to you, you cannot tell for sure. Maybe three days went by. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, you say now that maybe three days went by before you were moved from that first building to the room in the house. Is that what you're seriously suggesting now, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that I was unconscious and that I cannot tell for sure for how long, whether they beat me in the morning -- until morning or half night. That's why I said three days passed by, and I can't say for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that you were never given any reason for why you were being beaten. Do you stand by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did they never ask you any questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did ask questions. They told me, You have stayed in the company of Serbs, because they themselves stayed with Serbs day and night, and they accused me of staying with Serbs. I was a farmer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You were a farmer with a pistol. What were you doing with a pistol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. My father had permission to possess a pistol, then after some years I changed the papers and put it in my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You were driving a car and you had a pistol on you. When you reached the Serb roadblock, were you searched by the Serb police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did they ask to see your papers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They stopped me, saw me - I was with my family - and told me not to go that way, so I turned back.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: They didn't ask to see your driver's licence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you know any of the Serb police officers who stopped you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And did they tell you to go back because there was a risk of there being a KLA roadblock?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told me, You shouldn't go this way with your family. Better go home. It's not good to drive in this area. So I was obliged to go back in the direction of my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And when you were stopped at the UCK roadblock, you were searched there, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And they found the pistol on you; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you told them that you had a licence for the pistol. Did you show them the licence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took it along with the licence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Why were you carrying a pistol with you in the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just carrying it. I had a licence to carry it and I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Was that a police-issued pistol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And to whom did the police issue that pistol, reserve policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the Albanian police were there, I had a permission, and then I had it also when the Serbian police took over.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you have a photograph album in your car when you were stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you have any photographs --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only of film [Realtime transcript read in error, "Hil"], only of film. Yes, I had a photo with a friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And the translation we have on the screen is: "Only of Hil." Is Hil the name of the friend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you saying?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: This is a misunderstanding. I think it was only a film. This is what I understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's also what I thought I heard.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said a film.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You had a photograph of yourself with a friend. Was that friend a police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a retired police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You knew quite a lot of police officers, didn't you, Witness 6?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you got into the Opel Kadett, you found some photographs there, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the person whose car was held.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And as soon as you saw those photographs, you recognised that person, didn't you, you recognised him as Nenad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, his name was Nenad. He was working as a traffic policeman. I could recognise him because, when I went to Gjakove, I had seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, you had not just seen him, you knew what village he lived in, a little village near Klina; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How did you know that he lived in that village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Albanian policeman had told me where he was from.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, which Albanian policeman told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name is Zokan Kuqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And when did you have that conversation with Zokan Kuqi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used to have contact with him frequently. He was a commander in our area. Two years before the war started, he retired and he was the one who knew him better. He told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Is that the one who was in the photograph with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the clock. At the same time, I would like to seek one clarification. You said you had a photograph with you with a friend, a retired police officer. On that photograph, was that retired police officer portrayed in uniform or in civilian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Harvey, could you give us any further indication at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's difficult. I will spend the next break doing what I can to cut down on the questions. Your Honour will appreciate that this witness speaks to a significant number of victims who are laid at my client's door, and Your Honour, I know, will appreciate that I have been pretty quiet until now. But these are issues that I can't pass over lightly, and I am trying to keep the detail down to a reasonable minimum, and I've cut out quite a bit already, and I will, as I say, attempt to trim as much as I can during the current break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I think, realistically, I'm going to need about another 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will -- yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I indicate I've given some thought to the time estimate that I gave to Your Honours before the break, and I -- I think I can shave it down to 25 minutes; it was 40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That still means that we couldn't finish today unless Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I will be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Guy-Smith, unless you go to the minus eight or the minus ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't know if I could go down to minus eight, but I probably could go up to plus three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Harvey -- of course I see Mr. Di Fazio is also on his feet. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm just saying that my re-examination has probably gone from a few minutes now to maybe just a few more minutes, possibly eight minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, the Chamber will consider whether the 40 minutes you said you would need, whether -- in full respect for the fact that you, until now, have not taken much time with the cross-examination. At the same time, sometimes where you didn't take it, it was on the basis of an understanding among Defence counsel how to divide the time. So therefore, it's acknowledged that you're right, and at the same time I add this footnote to your observation. We'll have a break and we'll resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, the Chamber invites you to finish in 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'll do my best to accept your invitation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you left Jabllanice, Pal was walking around and his health was improving. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And he had the freedom that you had to walk around in the -- the grounds of the barracks. Is that what you've told us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you met Jabllanice, were there any other people whom you would describe as prisoners still being held in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only Pal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And how many soldiers, approximately, stayed in the barracks while you were there, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what to tell you about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Would it be more than 50 or less than 50?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three of them would come and beat you, and then ten or 15 others would come. People were coming and going. They were always on the move. I don't know what to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Different numbers at different times while you were there. What was the largest number that you would say, approximately, you recall being in the barracks at any time while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they would go towards Albania to get weapons, there could be a hundred or 200 of them there that I saw when they came to eat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How did you know they were going to Albania to get weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They talked amongst each other, and I also asked Gani and he told me that they were going to get weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You did tell one of the ICTY -- or one of the Office of the Prosecutor's investigators that -- these words: "I was working in the kitchen, too, during my last two weeks of my imprisonment." Now, first of all, is that correct, that you did say you were working in the kitchen for two weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not work in the kitchen. I washed-up in the meadow outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about how you came to make your first statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. How did they get in touch with you or how did you get in touch with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will be -- it would be a long story to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: If it has to be long, it has to be long. Let's try and keep it as short as we can. When was the first approach made, and was it made by you or was it made to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Albanian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Who in the Albanian police approached you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came to the house, they broke down the door, and they found some bullets of the gun that the KLA had taken from me, and they were asking me to give them that gun again; I mean the Albanian police. They also had with them Spanish KFOR soldiers. They wanted me to give them the same gun that had been already taken from me. I didn't want to tell them anything, and they still insisted. And I showed them the documents that I had been given, the papers I had been given in Jabllanice, and that's how it all started.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When do you say that took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately after the war and also in 2002. I was searched twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And when were you first asked to go to or to meet with investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor? When were you first asked that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came and asked me, Are you this and that person? And I said, Yes, and I explained the story and we continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: My question, sir, was: When did this happen?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And where did it happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How did you come to be in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had been called to go and give the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Were you called by telephone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they came to my place and we spoke orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Who came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know them, but they were in UNMIK car or maybe UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How many of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And was that the same person who interviewed you in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know his name. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm not asking you for his name, sir. I'm asking: Is the same person who came to your house the same person who then interviewed you when you went to Prizren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it was another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How soon after the person came to your house did you go to Prizren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About a week later, but I'm not sure. I'm not hundred per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did they come to your house to give you a -- to drive you to Prizren or did you have to go there under your own -- in your own car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went by bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And how many days did you stay in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not stay for days. I stayed for two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And was this the only time you went to Prizren in connection with making a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there about two times.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And when you were taken, were you taken into an office to meet the investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And how many people were there in the office while the interview took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: There was you, there was the investigator. Was there an interpreter present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So that's three people in the room. Anybody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you were being questioned by the investigator, did you -- did the investigator use a computer to take notes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You've already told the Trial Chamber this morning that you were shown a picture on a computer. You recall the computer, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the picture that I signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: My question was: You recall that there was a computer, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. There was a computer, but I don't know whether they were doing anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you recall if there was a tape recorder?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, only the interpreter interpreted, and I don't know beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you recall if there was a videocamera in the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: While you and the -- while you and the investigator were speaking, did the investigator write down any notes on a notepad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a simple notebook and he was writing in his handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you recall on a later date that you went to Pristina to look at some photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You saw photographs in the office of the investigator in Pristina, it was the same investigator, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have the same person twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Perhaps we could have 3D010092 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And while that's coming up, I have a couple more questions for you, Witness. You recall when you went to look at some photographs - whoever the investigator was - you remember seeing photographs, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did look at photographs. I have to look at them now again, though, because if I don't have them here, I don't know what to tell you about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm just looking to see what you remember for a moment. Do you recall being shown a number of boards or pieces of paper that had eight photographs of different people on them? Do you recall being shown a number of boards that had several photographs on them and being asked to see if you could pick out anybody in those photographs? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: What were you told about those boards? We'll call them photo-boards. What did the investigator tell you to do in relation to those photo-boards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognised the people who were in Jabllanice, the soldiers. Some of them I did not recognise. Whoever I recognised, I pointed at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Again, sir, my question was quite specific. What did the investigator tell you to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. Nothing. He didn't order me to do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Before he showed you the boards, did he explain what he was going to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did he give you any instructions about what you should do if you recognised somebody on the boards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want you to cast your mind back. Before that day when you went to see the investigator in Pristina, before then and after your release from Jabllanice, had you ever seen a photograph of Nazmi Brahimaj in between those two times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Had -- in any of your conversations with any police officer, had you ever been shown photographs of any of the people from Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which police?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The police in Gjakove, the Serb police.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't. They didn't give me any specifications when I was in Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did the UNMIK police ever show you any photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So apart from the investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor, did anybody ever show you any photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked me whether I knew the persons, if I looked at their photos, and I said yes when I -- some of them I recognised, some of them I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: My question, sir, was whether, apart from that investigator, did anybody else ever show you any photographs in relation to Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Okay. When you were shown the photo-boards, do you recall whether you were sitting down at a table or were you standing up or how -- how were you positioned when you looked at them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sitting. I was sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And in relation to where you were sitting, sir, where was the investigator who was giving you the photo-boards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was across of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So he was sitting on the other side of the table facing you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Were you asked to mark the photo-boards in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Were you asked to mark the photo-boards in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They simply -- I was simply asked who -- whether I knew any of them, and, if I did, I put a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So the investigator said to you, If you know any of them, put a number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Then, I'm sorry, please explain again what it is the investigator said you should do in relation to those photo-boards.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had the numbers there at the end of the photos, and I indicated that this number is a certain person. I mentioned the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And did the investigator ask you to either put a mark against the photograph or to write your name alongside the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked at the photographs, and then I signed at the number of the person that I recognised.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And when you did that, what did the investigator say, if anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Apart from the photo-boards, you were also shown some individual photographs to see if you could recognise people who had been in Jabllanice with you, people, for instance, like Pal Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I would like the witness to be shown, but not on the public screen, 65 ter 787, if we can have that up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you remember being shown this photo-board, Witness 6?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I don't want you to give a name right now, but do you recall identifying number 2 on that photo-board?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And did you say that that was somebody that you had known from your time in school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And did you say that that was somebody --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Or perhaps out of caution we should be in private session just for this question.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Witness, it is not challenged that you correctly identified both Nazmi Brahimaj and Lahi Brahimaj on the two separate photo-boards that you were shown with their pictures on them. I wish to make that clear. However, there are a number of points that I need to make to you. Number 1, Lahi Brahimaj was not present when -- on the evening when you were brought to Jabllanice the first time, was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Number 2, Lahi Brahimaj did visit the barracks very occasionally during the six weeks that you were there, but he was not there frequently.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To me it seemed he was there every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Number 3, Lahi Brahimaj never once touched you physically while you were in Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Number 4, Lahi Brahimaj --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- let's try to have this clarified. The question was -- Mr. Harvey put it to you that Lahi Brahimaj never once touched you physically. And your answer was: "I know he was there," but the question was whether he ever touched you physically.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He did. He maltreated me, he and his brother, continuously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And the fourth point I was going to put to you, Witness, is that he was never present on any occasion when anybody else maltreated you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I try to ... Mr. Harvey asked you whether Lahi Brahimaj -- whether -- when -- let me just have a look. Lahi Brahimaj, was he ever present when you were maltreated by other persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he was, he and Nazmija.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Witness, you told this Tribunal yesterday -- I'm sorry, on Friday that you had fractures, in the plural, as a result of the beatings that you received. Do you stand by that, more than one fracture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What fractures?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] That's what I'm asking you. Fractures of bones, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you guide us, Mr. Harvey, as to the exact --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had one fracture, and I have a scar on my right arm, and I still feel pain to this day. My skin was cut open. I had injuries on my arms, on my legs, everything hurts, my kidneys, my lungs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, you asked for guidance, unfortunately --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I found it. I found it, meanwhile; that's page 5210, line 8, I take it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was beaten on my legs, arms, I had fractures on my body, I have bruises on my back."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So, Witness, one fracture or more than one fracture, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One, only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] And when you gave your first statement to the ICTY -- to the OTP investigator on the 26th and 28th of November of 2002, you said this: "I was beaten with a bat on my arms, legs, and on my back very badly and I still have injuries, a small fracture on my right shoulder due to the beating." Is that what you told the investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it's translated wrongly. I have my -- I have a wound on my right side, but the fracture on my left side -- left arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you have a small fracture on your right shoulder?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have only pains.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And where do you say you have a fracture? Can you please point to it so we can see where you mean.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, on this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Pointing to the left lower forearm near the wrist on the outside aspect, towards the outside aspect of the left lower forearm. Do you have any idea how it came to be recorded that you mentioned only a small fracture on your right shoulder and nothing to do with your left forearm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fracture is on my left arm, but the injury is on my left shoulder --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction: Right shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see the time. I'm very nearly done and I recognise that I have gone over what you have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you have not followed my invitation, and you went even beyond what you indicated before. But before I give you an opportunity to do so, let me -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar has inquired into possibilities to finish, and we -- I'm not in a position anymore to ask such things, but I do understand that the teams we need, if we could finish within one hour from now on, that - and I think that should be possible; Mr. Di Fazio, I'm also looking at you - then you would have another three, four minutes to finish, Mr. Harvey, and then we could continue at this moment without a break, but I do of course not know whether any of the other ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might, Your Honour, I have another hearing that's starting tomorrow. I have an appointment to see my client, which had previously been set for this morning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- and now has been set for this afternoon at 2.30. I must see him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we try to arrange it in such a way that you are leaving the last 15 minutes and have done and perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: One would hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that co-counsel could take over those 15 minutes. Yes, Mr. Harvey, I'm really urging you now to finish very quickly. I mean, a lot of discussions about small fractures, and yes, of course, small and big fractures; fracture is a fracture, usually. But please proceed and finish in a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not the size of the fracture, it's the location and, of course, the accuracy because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Mr. Harvey, I do understand that, but, of course, you were wise enough not to further inquire into what the witness's knowledge was of the size of the kitchen here, for example. Well, there are -- of course, sometimes people use expressions which shouldn't be taken literally by the meaning. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Witness, you used the expression twice on Friday to describe members or people who joined the KLA, you described them as arrogant. Is that your view generally of people who were in -- who were in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were such against me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You spoke of your -- when you were asked about your own village and whether your co-villagers supported or opposed the KLA, you said: "Maybe some of the arrogant ones were mobilised." Now, these were not people who were arrogant towards you. This is just a term that you used to describe anybody who joins the KLA, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the bad ones I call like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'd like if we could have P335 on the screen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, I checked the -- both the sources of arrogance here, and to say that the way in which you put the question was properly reflecting the testimony of the witness last Friday is questionable. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you. If Your Honour finds it questionable, certainly in relation to what the witness said of his co-villagers, in my submission, and I quoted that accurately --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Maybe some of the arrogant ones were, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Some, yes. These others were arrogant as well so that does not qualify KLA members, and earlier he said something, his own arrogance compared to the arrogance of others. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You see in front of you, Witness, a document that you were given by Nazmi Brahimaj when you left Jabllanice. As you can see, it is signed clearly with his name, and so from the 25th of July onwards you had no difficulty knowing that Nazmi Brahimaj was one of the people in that camp. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try to explain it to you. What Mr. Harvey tells you is the following. Looking at this document, where clearly the name of Nazmi Brahimaj appears, you could have known on from the moment that you received this document that the name of the person that issued this document was Nazmi Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, you said that you learned about names only later.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. During the last two weeks when I was with Gani Brahimaj and I asked him about names and other things that I was interested in, and he told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You were angry that they held on to your car, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That car had cost you -- I think you said 30.000 Swiss francs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. When I bought it, it cost that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Our exchange rates vary, but would that have been about the equivalent of about 45.000 American dollars, do you know, at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the exchange rate is with dollars.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
